walkthroughs.body_html:
Before 1914, Europe was split into two big groups of allies.

The four long-term causes are remembered as MAIN: Militarism, Alliances, Imperialism, Nationalism.

The trigger came in June 1914: a Serbian shot Archduke Franz Ferdinand of Austria-Hungary. Within weeks, the alliances pulled most of Europe into war. ⚔️

On the Western Front in France and Belgium, soldiers dug long lines of trenches.

Between them lay No Man's Land — barbed wire, shell holes and mud. Going 'over the top' meant facing machine guns.

Trenches were filled with rats, lice and rainwater. Diseases like 'trench foot' were common. Many soldiers suffered shell shock. 😢

Big battles included Verdun and the Somme in 1916. On the first day of the Somme, the British army lost about 57,000 men.

In 1917 the USA joined the war. In 1918 Germany ran out of soldiers and food.

The fighting stopped at 11 a.m. on 11 November 1918 — the Armistice. We remember it every year on Remembrance Day. 🌺
